evidence.claim: The official bio states that Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo has been President of the Republic since 24 January 2019 and was elected on 30 December 2018.
evidence.title: Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo - Présidence RDC
evidence.excerpt: The official bio states that Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo has been President of the Republic since 24 January 2019 and was elected on 30 December 2018.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential biography; direct office-identification source.
evidence.period_fit: Direct office confirmation for the 2022 ruler-period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Official self-description of the office holder; useful for identity and tenure only.
contrary_evidence: Self-published and favorable; not independent verification of performance.

evidence.claim: The opposition boycotted the Assembly debate on electoral-law reform because it wanted first a consensus on reviewing CENI composition.
evidence.title: RDC: débat général ce vendredi à l'Assemblée nationale sur la réforme de la loi électorale
evidence.excerpt: The opposition boycotted the Assembly debate on electoral-law reform because it wanted first a consensus on reviewing CENI composition.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Congolese reporting on a concrete parliamentary process with named institutions and parties.
evidence.period_fit: Target year 2022; directly about the election-law environment Tshisekedi governed.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Tshisekedi's governing coalition and the institutional setup it oversaw, though the article reports opposition behavior rather than a presidential order.
contrary_evidence: Boycott itself does not prove unilateral manipulation, only that the process lacked broad trust.

evidence.claim: The state of siege was used to silence critics through arbitrary detention, military-court prosecutions, and violent suppression of protest.
evidence.title: DRC: One year on, 'State of Siege' used as a tool to crush dissent
evidence.excerpt: The state of siege was used to silence critics through arbitrary detention, military-court prosecutions, and violent suppression of protest.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed human-rights briefing with named incidents, interviews, and a clear description of the legal regime.
evidence.period_fit: Target year 2022, though the emergency regime began in 2021 and continued through 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Tshisekedi because he declared and repeatedly extended the state of siege and his appointed military/police authorities enforced it.
contrary_evidence: The stated rationale was civilian protection against armed groups, so the source is contesting effectiveness and legality rather than denying the security threat.

evidence.claim: Authorities threatened to crush protests and were using blanket bans and arrests under the state of siege to suppress accountability and dissent.
evidence.title: DRC: Stop using prolonged state of siege as excuse to crush protests
evidence.excerpt: Authorities threatened to crush protests and were using blanket bans and arrests under the state of siege to suppress accountability and dissent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights reporting focused on the same emergency regime and on named protest events.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Tshisekedi through the emergency regime and his appointed provincial and security authorities.
contrary_evidence: The protests were tied to eastern insecurity and M23/Rwanda-related anger, so the underlying grievance was not invented by the government.

evidence.claim: Military authorities in North Kivu and Ituri curtailed expression, broke up peaceful demonstrations with lethal force, and arbitrarily detained and prosecuted activists, journalists, and opposition members.
evidence.title: DR Congo: Martial Law Brings Crackdown in East
evidence.excerpt: Military authorities in North Kivu and Ituri curtailed expression, broke up peaceful demonstrations with lethal force, and arbitrarily detained and prosecuted activists, journalists, and opposition members.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Well-documented rights report by a major independent monitor with concrete examples and direct attribution.
evidence.period_fit: Target year 2022, with the emergency regime still in force.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed through Tshisekedi's declaration and maintenance of martial law and the conduct of authorities operating under his administration.
contrary_evidence: The source is critical and does not assess every area of the country equally; it focuses on the east and on documented incidents.

evidence.claim: The government did not restrict or disrupt internet access, though the report notes some monitoring of private online communications without clear legal authority.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Democratic Republic of the Congo
evidence.excerpt: The government did not restrict or disrupt internet access, though the report notes some monitoring of private online communications without clear legal authority.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official report with a narrow, concrete factual finding that is useful as favorable counterevidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to the national executive because it describes what Tshisekedi's government did and did not do on internet control.
contrary_evidence: The same section notes some monitoring of private online communications without appropriate legal authority.

evidence.claim: Police arrested, detained, and physically abused three journalists while they covered an opposition protest in Kinshasa.
evidence.title: DRC police detain, beat 3 journalists covering protest
evidence.excerpt: Police arrested, detained, and physically abused three journalists while they covered an opposition protest in Kinshasa.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialist monitor with named victims, date, location, and direct reporting from the journalists.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Tshisekedi because national police acted under his administration and the protest concerned opposition politics.
contrary_evidence: The report describes police conduct at one protest; it does not show a formal nationwide censorship order.

evidence.claim: Four military intelligence agents arrested and beat journalist Christophe Katembo Muthahinga over traffic coverage in North Kivu.
evidence.title: DRC military detains, beats journalist Christophe Katembo Muthahinga
evidence.excerpt: Four military intelligence agents arrested and beat journalist Christophe Katembo Muthahinga over traffic coverage in North Kivu.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct, contemporaneous press-freedom documentation with named perpetrators and victim.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the national military/intelligence chain under Tshisekedi's presidency, though the immediate perpetrators were lower-level officers.
contrary_evidence: The incident was local and does not by itself prove a central order to target that journalist.

evidence.claim: Republican Guard members raided Jean-Marc Kabund's house, and he resigned saying he had suffered bullying, humiliation, and torture.
evidence.title: Vice president of Congo's parliament resigns over bullying, humiliation
evidence.excerpt: Republican Guard members raided Jean-Marc Kabund's house, and he resigned saying he had suffered bullying, humiliation, and torture.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a concrete intra-elite coercion incident with direct quotations and named security forces.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Tshisekedi's political environment because the Republican Guard is a presidential force and Kabund was a key political figure in the governing camp turned critic.
contrary_evidence: The account is based on Kabund's description; the government and Guard declined comment in the report.

evidence.claim: Opposition leader Jean-Marc Kabund was arrested after controversy over remarks criticizing President Felix Tshisekedi.
evidence.title: Congo arrests opposition leader Kabund
evidence.excerpt: Opposition leader Jean-Marc Kabund was arrested after controversy over remarks criticizing President Felix Tshisekedi.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reporting on a politically salient arrest with named actor, date, and stated charge.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the national executive climate because the case centered on criticism of the president and was handled by state authorities.
contrary_evidence: The report says the charge was not fully specified at the time, so the exact legal basis remained contested.

evidence.claim: JED recorded 124 press-freedom violations in 2022, including arrests, assaults, kidnappings, and one journalist death.
evidence.title: RDC : 124 cas d'atteintes à la liberté de la presse dont un décès et 2 enlèvements documentés en 2022 (Rapport JED)
evidence.excerpt: JED recorded 124 press-freedom violations in 2022, including arrests, assaults, kidnappings, and one journalist death.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Local-language reporting of a specialist watchdog's annual tally, with concrete counts and categories.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Tshisekedi because the violations occurred under his presidency, though many incidents were provincial rather than ordered from Kinshasa.
contrary_evidence: The source is a report about violations, not an official government record or a court finding of central direction.

unresolved_gaps: No direct evidence of nuclear command-and-control, custody, accident-prevention, or safety-safeguard performance under Tshisekedi.
Independent compliance evidence for the Nairobi and Luanda processes remains thin.
Direct command-responsibility evidence and remedy follow-up for police and military abuses are still weak.
Direct evidence on institutional strengthening, political equality, and election-body independence is thin.
Independent 2022 implementation and household-level outcome evidence is still thin.
Direct ruler-attributable outcome data on health, education, nutrition, and protection remains sparse.
Direct evidence of Tshisekedi's own assets, family/business interests, campaign finance, and false statements is missing.
Completed outputs and adaptation under failure are not well documented for the major 2022 programs.
